# Aindle

> A private, read-only AI work board for a desk — or a jailbroken Kindle Oasis 1 lock screen.

Aindle is self-hosted. The public website is an introduction plus mock demos. The hub stays on your LAN or Tailscale. It shows quotas, 24h/7d token spend, and in-progress / awaiting-confirmation / background tasks. It does not track productivity, approve work on the Kindle, or display prompts, replies, paths, or secrets.

## Start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Octo-o-o-o/aindle.git
cd aindle
npm install
npm run hub
```

Then open:

- Desktop: http://127.0.0.1:8787/monitor.html
- Lock-screen HTML: http://127.0.0.1:8787/eink.html?page=local
- Lock-screen PNG: http://127.0.0.1:8787/dash.png?page=local

The hub seeds mock data so the screen is not empty. Live machines:

```bash
npx aindle init --local
# edit ./config/registry.yaml — keep only tools you use
npx aindle agent --loop 60
```

Optional Kindle Oasis 1: copy `kindle/oasis1/` to `/mnt/us/aindle`, set `HUB` in `hub.env` to the LAN URL (never `127.0.0.1` on the device), start from KUAL, then lock.

## What it is not

Not a public SaaS. Not a TokenTracker / OctoMonitor fork. Not a billing invoice. Not a scoreboard. Unlocking the Kindle returns the stock reader.
